about.text: Tarak-juk is a Korean porridge of milk and finely ground glutinous rice, seasoned with salt and sometimes honey. The rice is soaked, ground and sieved, its settled deposit is boiled, and the milk is stirred in slowly over low heat. It was royal court food in the Joseon period, when the milk came from the royal dairy at Naksan.
